quotes.text: None of this happens because people are careless. It happens because the systems ask people to become the connection.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes duplicate data as a system design problem rather than a people problem.

quotes.text: A connection can move a change very quickly. If nobody agreed who owns that change, it can move a mistake just as quickly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for clear record ownership before switching on live sync.

quotes.text: A record should move, because people need the same operational record in both places, not because copying data feels safer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A simple test for deciding which tables belong in a dual-write setup.

quotes.text: Because duplicate records, incomplete addresses, and old test data don't magically clean themselves up just because the sync starts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Retrying a failed record without fixing the cause usually just creates the same failure again.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

chapters.title: What data moves and who owns it

takeaways: Dual-write keeps selected shared records such as customers, addresses and products in near real-time sync between Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps and Dataverse.
Table maps define what moves and in which direction, so every shared record needs an agreed owner before the connection goes live.
Clean data before the initial sync, check existing integrations, and monitor logs and alerts instead of blindly retrying failed records.
hook: Sales updates a customer address, but finance still sees the old one. This episode explains to Dynamics 365 users and consultants how dual-write connects finance and operations apps with Dataverse-based customer apps. You will learn what data moves, who should own it and which mistakes to avoid.
